chunks: [Allah the Exalted] Blessed is Allah, He whom the height of aspirations cannot reach
and the subtlety of intellects cannot attain Him
The First, He who has no limit so that He might be contained within it
and no end for Him so that He might cease
ai.seo_question: How does Nahj al-Balagha describe Allah's transcendence and infinity?
ai.summary: In this passage from Nahj al-Balagha, Imam Ali (AS) articulates the doctrine of divine transcendence (Tanzih), asserting that Allah's essence is beyond the grasp of human intellect (Fitan) and ambition. He describes Him as the First (Al-Awwal) without a beginning and the Last (Al-Akhir) without an end, a concept deeply rooted in Shia theological discussions on God's infinity and simplicity. This eulogy serves as a foundational reminder of God's incomparability, distinguishing His eternal nature from created beings.

en.sayed-ali-raza: Exalted is Allāh Whom heights of daring cannot approach
and fineness of intelligence cannot find.
He is such First that there is no extremity for Him so that He be contained within it,
nor is there an end for Him where He would cease.
